text.p: A country with a history of failed army coups should prepare for another military adventure -- so said a statement circulating in Philippine military camps on Thursday.

Purportedly coming from a group calling itself "Filipino Soldiers for the Nation", the statement said the group would launch a coup if Defence Secretary and retired general Renato de Villa was not elected president in next year's elections to succeed Fidel Ramos.

"If necessary, in the name of peace and development, the SPPB will not hesitate to launch a military action in support of General de Villa," said the statement issued in the name of "Captain Jose Salvacion".
Officials said there was no such person in the military roster and no such group existed in the military.
A senior military officer said the statement was apparently circulated by political enemies of de Villa, who has expressed interest in running for president next year.
Ramos, whose six-year term ends in June 1998, is barred from standing for re-election under the constitution which limits a president to only one term.
The Philippines was rocked by six unsuccessful army coups between 1986 and 1989 when Corazon Aquino was president.
